chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muawiya ibn Hukaym, from Abu Malik al-Hadrami, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'I send the dog and say Bismillah over it, and it hunts, but I do not have with me what to slaughter it with.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Leave it until it kills it, and eat.'

key_terms.أُسَمِّي عَلَيْهِ: I say Bismillah over it (invoking God's name)
key_terms.مَا أُذَكِّيهِ بِهِ: What I use to slaughter it (with)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat hunted by a dog if I don't have a knife to slaughter it myself?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the mechanism of *dhabh* (ritual slaughter) for game hunted by dogs, ruling that the animal's own killing suffices even without the hunter's immediate invocation or knife. This establishes the principle that the dog's bite constitutes the valid slaughter provided the hunter has named Allah, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the act of the hunting animal, coupled with the hunter's intention, validates the meat. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the hunter's role and the predator's action in determining permissibility.
